claim: For integers \(N\ge 3\) and \(2\le m\le N-1\), let \(F_N=(\omega^{rs})_{r,s\in\mathbb Z_N}\) with \(\omega=e^{-2\pi i/N}\), and select the three rows \(\mathcal M=\{0,1,m\}\). The resulting \(3\times N\) harmonic frame is full spark if and only if \(\gcd(N,m)\le 2\) and \(\gcd(N,m-1)\le 2\); equivalently, it is full spark if and only if \(\mathcal M\) is uniformly distributed over every divisor of \(N\).

correctness.rationale: Every singular minor is normalized to S_m(u)=S_m(v). If the common value is zero, three common N-th and m-th roots force gcd(N,m)>=3. If nonzero, conjugation gives u^(m-1)=v^(m-1)=a and exact cross-multiplication forces a=1, hence gcd(N,m-1)>=3. Converse subgroup witnesses are explicit. The packaged exact checker verifies the determinant identity, divisor equivalence, and thousands of witness cases.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete, elementary iff criterion for a natural infinite two-parameter family of three-row harmonic frames and proves that the standard divisor-uniformity necessity is sufficient throughout this family, including composite non-prime-power orders. The test reduces to two gcd computations and strictly generalizes the previously established m=4 case.
